prerequisites: Python, and reading a JSON Schema. No prior agent or LangChain experience is assumed.
objectives: Build an agent loop by hand and say what each part is for: model call, tool call, observation, stopping condition
Decide when a fixed workflow beats an agent, and justify it
Map each hand-built part to its LangChain equivalent: @tool schemas, messages, structured output, callbacks
Show observability, traceability, governance, and evaluation working in the loop from the first line, not bolted on later
lessons: The loop by hand: tools as schemas, the model turn, feeding results back, and stopping
The loop in LangChain: what the framework generates for you, and what it must not take over
The four threads: spans, one trace id, an allowlist enforced in code, and outcome-first grading
agent-foundations-tutor.local_lab: Run uv run pytest tests/unit/foundations -q, then read src/foundations/agent_loop.py beside langchain_loop.py and list every job the framework took over and every job it did not. Then take two tasks, one whose steps are all known in advance (fetch a curve, interpolate at 5 years, format a table) and one whose next step depends on what a tool returns, and write down for each whether a fixed workflow or the agent loop fits, and what the loop would add in cost and nondeterminism.
agent-foundations-tutor.failure_lab: Script a model turn that sends malformed arguments and one that requests place_order. Predict the tool message, the audit record, and the span status for each before running them.
agent-foundations-tutor.build_lab: Add a second allowed tool to demo_tools() with a hand-written JSON Schema, then the same tool with @tool in langchain_loop.py. Write a test that a malformed call returns an error to the model, and one that a run whose allowlist omits the tool writes a denied audit record carrying the run's trace id.
agent-foundations-tutor.assessment: Explain the agent loop without notes, including why governance and evaluation are part of it, and name what LangChain generates versus what stays in your code.

prerequisites: Agent foundations, or working experience of the agent loop, tool calling, and structured output
Read README.md and ARCHITECTURE.md
objectives: Separate agents, workflows, tools, skills, and controls
Design bounded context and delegation paths
Explain retries, checkpoints, interrupts, and recovery
agent-architecture-tutor.local_lab: Trace one request through src/context, src/agents, and tests; draw the state transitions.
agent-architecture-tutor.failure_lab: Inject a specialist timeout and explain retry, call limits, checkpoint, and dead-letter behavior.
agent-architecture-tutor.build_lab: Add a fourth specialist to src/agents/multi_agent.py with its own non-overlapping tool tuple and prompt, wire it through specialist_subagents(), and add a test proving the orchestrator can delegate to it and that it cannot reach another specialist's tools.
agent-architecture-tutor.assessment: Teach the architecture without notes and map five components to their trust boundaries.

prerequisites: Read the agent architecture tutor first
objectives: Explain graph state, reducers, conditional edges, subagents, persistence, and interrupts
Trace native Deep Agents delegation, and say what it builds on your behalf
Design safe retry and resume behavior
lessons: Graph and state model: schema, reducers, and what last-write-wins costs you
Subagents and tools, and the same shape built from primitives
langgraph-deep-agents-tutor.local_lab: Trace a multi-agent request and inspect the checkpoint/resume tests, then read handbuilt_graph.py beside multi_agent.py and name what create_deep_agent generated for you.
langgraph-deep-agents-tutor.failure_lab: Crash Quant after Macro completes and explain why completed work is preserved.
langgraph-deep-agents-tutor.build_lab: Extend src/agents/handbuilt_graph.py so two specialists run concurrently and both contribute findings, then remove the operator.add reducer. Predict the failure before you run it: LangGraph refuses the concurrent write with InvalidUpdateError rather than quietly keeping one branch -- the opposite of the sequential overwrite. Building the failure is the lab; both behaviours are already pinned in the tests.
langgraph-deep-agents-tutor.assessment: Compare a hand-built graph, Deep Agent, and supervisor pattern for one workflow.

prerequisites: Agent foundations: the agent loop, tool calling, and the allowlist in governed_call
objectives: Explain MCP's primitives and who controls each, and the two standard transports
Explain the 2026-07-28 stateless protocol, and how it differs from the earlier initialize handshake the SDK still speaks in legacy mode
Tell protocol errors from tool execution errors, and say which ones the model sees
Separate authentication from authorization at an MCP boundary, and keep observability and audit continuous across it
lessons: The protocol: primitives, JSON-RPC, transports, and stateless per-request metadata
The boundary: errors the model can act on, untrusted descriptions, and why identity must be authenticated, not asserted
Across the boundary: two layers of governance, one trace id, and the agent loop calling tools over MCP
mcp-tutor.local_lab: Run uv run pytest tests/unit/mcp_server -q, then read src/mcp_server/client_lab.py and trace one tools/call from the agent loop through the SDK to server.py and back, naming each span and each authorization decision.
mcp-tutor.failure_lab: Call risk_metrics for PORT_B as PM_USER, call a tool that does not exist, and call a server bound to PM_USER while claiming RISK_USER in _meta. Predict for each whether it is a protocol or a tool execution error, what the model would see, and which spec rule or SDK behaviour applies; then check against test_client_lab.py.
mcp-tutor.build_lab: Add the HTTP counterpart of the stdio identity binding: a verifier that accepts a bearer token only if its audience is this server, and binds the identity from the token's subject. Write tests that a token issued for another audience is refused (no token passthrough), that a valid token's identity is what Cedar authorizes, and that a _meta claim still cannot override it.
mcp-tutor.assessment: Explain MCP without notes, including why a tool description grants nothing, why claimed identity is not authentication, and how one trace id covers both sides of the boundary.

prerequisites: Read the observability module and one agent trace
objectives: Explain traces and metrics as distinct signals, and say which question each one answers
Choose between a counter and a histogram, and propagate context across a process boundary
Design cost-aware, privacy-safe telemetry and sample without producing traces with holes in them
Correlate application, audit, and evaluation evidence
lessons: Telemetry primitives: traces, spans, and why metrics are a separate signal
Instrumentation: semantic attributes, counters and histograms, context propagation
opentelemetry-tutor.local_lab: Trace an API request through authorization, analytics, and audit spans, then record the same run through an InMemoryMetricReader and read the points back out.
opentelemetry-tutor.failure_lab: Remove raw prompts and holdings from a proposed span schema while preserving diagnosability, then explain what a plain TraceIdRatioBased sampler does to that trace and why ParentBased fixes it.
opentelemetry-tutor.build_lab: Instrument an uninstrumented function with a span and a metric, justifying every attribute against the privacy rule, then assert the recorded points with an InMemoryMetricReader. Any attribute you cannot justify is one you should not be emitting.
opentelemetry-tutor.assessment: Design a trace schema and justify every attribute, exporter, and redaction rule.

prerequisites: Read evals/, config/eval-baseline.json, and observability notes
objectives: Design independent evaluation dimensions
Interpret regression and repeated-run results
Separate automated scores from human review
evaluation-agentops-tutor.local_lab: Add or inspect a case with routing, tool, argument, answer, and policy expectations.
evaluation-agentops-tutor.failure_lab: Investigate a case that passes answer quality but fails policy or citation coverage.
evaluation-agentops-tutor.build_lab: Write a new evaluator dimension in scripts/run_eval.py, add a golden case that exercises it as a stub, and state what score movement on that one case would mean given the active case count. Then explain what would have to be true before you flip it from stub to active.
evaluation-agentops-tutor.assessment: Write a promotion decision that includes quality, safety, stability, cost, and evidence.

prerequisites: Read the security model and CI workflow map
objectives: Separate AuthN, AuthZ, guardrails, and tool enforcement
Test policy and prompt-injection boundaries
Explain release, rollback, approval, and teardown evidence
governance-delivery-tutor.local_lab: Run the authorization and guardrail suites and classify each enforcement layer.
governance-delivery-tutor.failure_lab: Attempt role spoofing, portfolio bypass, output exfiltration, and a disguised write.
governance-delivery-tutor.build_lab: Add a role to config/roles.yaml with a Cedar policy granting it exactly one tool, then write the adversarial test proving it cannot reach a second one. The test that matters is the one that fails if the policy is too generous.
governance-delivery-tutor.assessment: Produce a release review that names controls, residual risks, and rollback evidence.

prerequisites: Fixed-income fundamentals - bond pricing, duration, DV01, spread duration. Learn or revise them in pm-mechanics; this course assumes them rather than teaching them.
Read this repository's fixed-income analytics and their tests
objectives: Trace how this repository turns bond terms and a curve into a price, and what each tool returns as evidence
Judge whether a fixed-income tool result is trustworthy given its stated inputs, assumptions, and mock flag
Recognise when an agent is inventing terms it was never given, and return needs_review instead
lessons: The fixed-income tool surface: what each function takes, returns, and refuses
Reading a result as evidence: assumptions, provenance, vintage, and the mock flag
Failure modes: missing terms, stale vintages, and ticker-only valuation requests
ficc-tutor-agent.local_lab: Run scripts/run_depth_exercise.py and reconcile price, duration, key-rate DV01, and provenance.
ficc-tutor-agent.failure_lab: Reject incomplete bond terms, stale data, and ticker-only valuation requests.
ficc-tutor-agent.build_lab: Add a fixed-income analytic this repo lacks -- spread duration on a position, or carry over a horizon -- with a JSON Schema contract and a test whose expected value you computed by hand first, not from the code you just wrote.
ficc-tutor-agent.assessment: Explain a synthetic bond portfolio review with assumptions, units, and limitations.

prerequisites: Portfolio theory - mean-variance, the efficient frontier, risk parity. Learn or revise them in pm-mechanics; this course assumes them.
Read this repository's optimizer and its tests
objectives: Trace how a method, constraints, and a covariance matrix become a proposal this repository will defend
Evaluate a proposal on turnover, transaction cost, concentration, and feasibility rather than on weights alone
Explain why an infeasible proposal fails loudly for a human to resolve instead of being silently relaxed
lessons: The optimizer tool surface: methods, institutional limits, and input validation
Turning weights into a reviewable proposal: deltas, turnover, cost, concentration
Where it stops: infeasibility, the proposal/execution boundary, and the unbuilt next layer
portfolio-construction-tutor.local_lab: Run an allocation on supplied inputs and perturb covariance or constraints.
portfolio-construction-tutor.failure_lab: Create infeasible, concentrated, or high-turnover proposals and explain the safe result.
portfolio-construction-tutor.build_lab: Add a constraint to src/analytics/optimizer.py that rejects rather than silently relaxing, with a test proving an infeasible request raises instead of returning quietly adjusted weights. A minimum position size works from the existing weight_bounds; a sector cap is the harder and more instructive version, because optimize_portfolio receives no sector data at all -- you have to thread the metadata through the signature and update the tool contract to match.
portfolio-construction-tutor.assessment: Present an allocation proposal with assumptions, sensitivity, costs, and human approval requirements.

prerequisites: Read the provenance module and public-data catalog
objectives: Distinguish observation, publication, filing, retrieval, and decision times
Apply point-in-time eligibility
Handle stale, conflicting, and uncertain evidence
data-provenance-research-tutor.local_lab: Create two vintages and select the record eligible for a historical decision.
data-provenance-research-tutor.failure_lab: Submit stale, conflicting, incomplete, and unlicensed evidence and classify each outcome.
data-provenance-research-tutor.build_lab: Add a connector that returns a provenance envelope with observation_date and vintage, plus a test that a decision dated before the vintage cannot read it. The point-in-time rule has to be enforced by your code, not by convention.
data-provenance-research-tutor.assessment: Produce a cited research bundle that states what it proves and what it cannot prove.

prerequisites: Browse data/README.md and the public sample pack
objectives: Understand the decision use of each public source
Compare source timing, licensing, and identifiers
Distinguish fixture, connector-capable, and live evidence
investment-data-tutor.local_lab: Browse three sample sources and build a source comparison table.
investment-data-tutor.failure_lab: Reject a source that is stale, unlicensed, unresolved, or incorrectly treated as authoritative.
investment-data-tutor.build_lab: Add a public source to the data catalog with its licensing, timing, and identifier semantics recorded, plus a test asserting the fixture is labelled mock rather than live. A source you cannot describe the limits of does not belong in the catalog.
investment-data-tutor.assessment: Recommend evidence for a PM question while stating limitations and integration status.

prerequisites: Read the capstone and Devil's Advocate implementation
objectives: Separate thesis, evidence, dissent, and decision
Grade uncertainty and open questions
Keep committee review distinct from order execution
investment-committee-tutor.local_lab: Run a synthetic rates-and-credit committee review and identify required evidence.
investment-committee-tutor.failure_lab: Challenge unsupported certainty, missing evidence, and an attempted autonomous trade.
investment-committee-tutor.build_lab: Add a challenge to src/agents/devils_advocate.py that fires on a specific unsupported claim shape, with a test showing it triggers on a thesis missing its evidence and stays quiet on one that has it.
investment-committee-tutor.assessment: Write a balanced committee record with recommendation, dissent, conditions, and approval state.

prerequisites: Agent foundations: the agent loop, tool calling, and governed_call
objectives: Call a Bedrock model through the Converse API, and say what it standardises across models
Run client-side tool use, knowing the model only requests tools and your code runs them
Retry only what can succeed later, with bounded backoff and jitter, and scope IAM to exactly the model and inference profile in use
Use guardrails, prompt caching, and Knowledge Bases for what each actually does, and measure their effect honestly
lessons: Converse and tool use: one API across models, toolUse and toolResult, and the loop that stays yours
Operating it: throttling and retries, inference profiles, and least-privilege IAM
Around the model: guardrails as an API, prompt caching and its token accounting, and retrieval with citations
aws-bedrock-tutor.local_lab: Run uv run pytest tests/unit/runtime/test_bedrock_lab.py -q, then read src/runtime/bedrock_lab.py and trace one tool-use round trip: the Converse request, the toolUse block, governed_call, and the toolResult sent back in a user message.
aws-bedrock-tutor.failure_lab: With Stubber, script a ThrottlingException, an AccessDeniedException, and a guardrail_intervened turn. Predict for each whether with_retries retries it, what the loop returns, and which span attribute or audit record shows it; then check against test_bedrock_lab.py.
aws-bedrock-tutor.build_lab: Add ServiceUnavailableException handling evidence: a Stubber test that it is retried and then succeeds, and one that a ValidationException is not. Then write the least-privilege policy for a second inference profile with invoke_through_profile_policy and a test that it names each Region's model.
aws-bedrock-tutor.assessment: Explain what Bedrock does and does not do for an agent without notes: who runs tools, what to retry, what a guardrail can and cannot replace, and how to read cached token usage.

prerequisites: AWS Bedrock: Converse, IAM for model invocation, and inference profiles
Read the local AgentCore config and evidence ledger
objectives: Distinguish Runtime, Gateway, Identity, Policy, Memory, Evaluations, and Guardrails
Map local controls to hosted intent
Classify deployment, invocation, and cleanup evidence
aws-agentcore-tutor.local_lab: Map every config/agentcore.yaml field to a local implementation and evidence artifact.
aws-agentcore-tutor.failure_lab: Diagnose missing model access, IAM permission, and Gateway permission using recorded fixtures.
aws-agentcore-tutor.build_lab: Write a new entry for config/agentcore.yaml and the local runbook step that would deploy it, then add a fixture-backed test asserting the entrypoint contract without calling AWS. Deploying is not part of the lab; being able to say exactly what would be created is.
aws-agentcore-tutor.assessment: Explain a safe deploy-smoke-teardown plan without requesting credentials.

Carry identity and provenance from a Canvas action through the MCP boundary

lessons: Canvas actions over MCP (the protocol itself is taught in the MCP course)
copilot-canvas-mcp-tutor.local_lab: Trace a portfolio request from Canvas action to MCP authorization and deterministic tool output.
copilot-canvas-mcp-tutor.failure_lab: Attempt a cross-portfolio request through a mocked Canvas capability and document the denial.
copilot-canvas-mcp-tutor.build_lab: Add one tool to src/mcp_server/server.py with its JSON Schema contract in contracts/tools/, and a test proving an unentitled identity is refused at the MCP boundary rather than inside the tool.
copilot-canvas-mcp-tutor.assessment: Design a governed Canvas panel with state, evidence, approval, and failure visibility.

agent-development-lifecycle-tutor.failure_lab: Change a covered implementation path without updating its skill and predict the CI failure.
